text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bund futures jaunted higher in late trade, breaking free of key technical barriers to push above par for the first time since late March. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.28, up 0.98 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts chalked up solid gains in a day of thin volumes as German Bunds set the pace in Europe. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-01/32, up 12/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures climbed as optimism about European monetary union helped reverse some of the pessimism which has weighed on European bond markets since talk of a delay to the project surfaced recently. The June notionnel bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.18, up 1.08 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets powered higher as renewed optimism about the prospects for European monetary union, a stronger lira and a firmer Bund market gave them fresh upward impetus. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.59, up 1.99 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened firm, aided by a stronger dollar. "The main story is the dollar has been firmer," said David Sloan, senior economist at I.D.E.A. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-20/32, up 20/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.08 percent.

JAPAN - Cash yen bonds and futures were higher in late trade as sentiment remained strong. Traders said that given weak Tokyo stock prices, there were few investment alternatives. Newly launched domestic corporate straight bonds saw brisk sales on Monday, supporting Japanese government bonds. In after-hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 127.14, up 0.18 from Friday's settlement price in Tokyo.

EUROBONDS - The primary market sprang back to life after recent inertia with a flurry of dollar deals in the three-, four- and five-year sectors. A Helaba unit launched the largest bond, a $500 million five-year deal. United Parcel Services and Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing both tapped the four-year sector, while BNG and WestLB set three-year deals. Korea Development Bank launched a 150 million sterling three-year FRN. There was also activity in the Australian dollar, Canadian dollar, Czech crown and guilder currency sectors.
